examples.ko: 친구가 같이 놀러 가자고 자꾸 꼬드겨요.
examples.en: My friend keeps coaxing me to go out and play together.

examples.ko: 동생이 꼬드기는 바람에 아이스크림을 두 개나 먹었어요.
examples.en: Because my younger sibling talked me into it, I ate two ice creams.

examples.ko: 누가 너를 꼬드겨서 그런 일을 하게 했어요?
examples.en: Who coaxed you into doing something like that?

examples.ko: 직원이 비싼 옷을 사라고 계속 꼬드겼어요.
examples.en: The staff member kept coaxing me to buy the expensive clothes.
Don't tempt a child into doing bad things.
Don't even think about trying to sweet-talk me.

explain: '설득하다'와 달리 보통 상대가 하지 않아도 될 일이나 좋지 않은 일을 달콤한 말로 하게 만들 때 써요. 명사는 '꼬임'이고, 일상 대화에서는 '꼬시다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: Unlike '설득하다' (to persuade), it usually means getting someone to do something they needn't do, or something not good, with sweet words. The noun is '꼬임', and in everyday talk people also say '꼬시다'.

examples.en: Where do you think you're going looking like that?

examples.ko: 비를 맞고 온 꼬락서니가 정말 말이 아니네요.
examples.en: You look a complete mess after coming in from the rain.
He doesn't see how he looks himself and only criticizes others.

examples.ko: 밤새 놀다 들어온 꼬락서니 좀 보세요.
examples.en: Just look at the state of him coming home after playing all night.

examples.ko: 이 꼬락서니를 엄마가 보시면 놀라실 거예요.
examples.en: Mom will be shocked if she sees me looking like this.

examples.ko: 옷은 구겨지고 머리는 헝클어지고 꼬락서니도 엉망이에요.
examples.en: My clothes are wrinkled, my hair is messy, and I look awful overall.

explain: '꼴'을 낮잡아 이르는 말이라, 남의 모습이나 처지를 못마땅해하거나 한심하게 볼 때 써요. 그래서 상대 앞에서 쓰면 기분 나쁘게 들릴 수 있어요. 중립적으로 말하고 싶으면 '모습'을 쓰세요.
explain_en: It is a belittling way of saying '꼴' (shape, look), used when you disapprove of or look down on someone's appearance or state. So it can sound insulting to a person's face. For a neutral statement, use '모습'.

examples.en: The puppies are wriggling in their mother's arms.
A caterpillar is squirming on a leaf.
The baby wriggled its hands and feet under the blanket.

examples.ko: 개미 몇 마리가 바닥에서 꼬물거리는 게 보여요.
examples.en: I can see a few ants wriggling on the floor.
The tadpoles wriggling in the water are so cute.
Every time the baby squirms, I can't help smiling.

explain: 작고 귀여운 것이 천천히 움직일 때 써서 아기, 강아지, 올챙이, 애벌레에 잘 어울려요. '꼬물대다'도 같은 뜻이고 부사는 '꼬물꼬물'이에요.
explain_en: It is used for small, cute things moving slowly, so it suits babies, puppies, tadpoles and caterpillars. '꼬물대다' means the same, and the adverb is '꼬물꼬물'.

examples.ko: 아기 강아지들이 담요 위에서 꼬물꼬물 움직여요.
examples.en: The puppies are squirming around on the blanket.
A caterpillar is crawling along the leaf, wriggling.

examples.ko: 아기 고양이들이 꼬물꼬물 엄마 곁으로 모여요.
examples.en: The kittens gather around their mother, wriggling along.
I saw tadpoles wriggling along as they swam.

examples.ko: 꼬물꼬물 기어 오는 아기가 정말 귀여워요.
examples.en: The baby crawling toward me with little wriggles is so cute.
The ants are going along in a line, squirming.

explain: '꼬물거리다'의 부사로, 작고 귀여운 것이 천천히 자꾸 움직이는 모습에 써요. 손가락·발가락 같은 몸의 일부를 조금씩 움직일 때는 '꼼지락꼼지락'이 더 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is the adverb of '꼬물거리다', used for small, cute things moving slowly and repeatedly. When you move a part of the body, like fingers or toes, bit by bit, '꼼지락꼼지락' fits better.

examples.en: My grandmother's back is quite bent.

examples.ko: 철사 끝이 꼬부라져서 잘 안 들어가요.
examples.en: The end of the wire is bent, so it won't go in easily.
The road bends to the left up ahead.
I picked up a stick with a bent end.
As people get older, their backs can become stooped.

examples.ko: 머리카락 끝이 꼬부라지지 않게 펴 주세요.
examples.en: Please straighten it so the ends of the hair don't curl.

explain: '구부러지다'와 비슷한 말이에요. 허리, 철사, 길이 휘어진 모습에 쓰고, '꼬부랑 할머니'처럼 허리가 굽은 모습을 말할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It is similar to '구부러지다'. It describes a back, a wire or a road that bends, and it also appears in '꼬부랑 할머니', an old woman with a bent back.

examples.ko: 산 위로 가는 길이 꼬불꼬불 이어져 있어요.
examples.en: The road up the mountain winds on and on.
The alley was so winding that I got lost.
I got a perm yesterday, so my hair is all curly.
The child scribbled wavy letters on the paper.
The river winds its way to the sea.
I like the curly ramen noodles.

explain: '꾸불꾸불'보다 작고 가는 느낌으로, 좁은 길이나 가는 선, 파마머리, 라면 면발에 잘 어울려요. '꼬불꼬불한 길'처럼 뒤에 명사를 꾸밀 수도 있어요.
explain_en: It feels smaller and finer than '꾸불꾸불', and suits narrow paths, thin lines, permed hair and ramen noodles. You can also modify a noun with it, as in '꼬불꼬불한 길'.

examples.en: I fell for my friend's coaxing and skipped class.
That sweet temptation was actually a lie.

examples.ko: 아이들은 어른의 꼬임을 쉽게 알아채지 못해요.
examples.en: Children can't easily notice an adult's enticement.

examples.ko: 누구의 꼬임으로 이런 일을 했는지 말해 보세요.
examples.en: Tell me whose enticement led you to do this.
Enticement sounds like nice words at first.

examples.ko: 그 광고의 꼬임 때문에 필요 없는 물건을 샀어요.
examples.en: That ad tempted me into buying something I didn't need.

explain: '꼬임에 넘어가다', '꼬임에 빠지다'처럼 짝말로 외워 두면 편해요. 동사는 '꼬드기다'이고, 일상 대화에서는 '꼬시다'라고도 해요. 같은 글자의 '꼬임'이 실이나 줄이 꼬인 상태를 가리킬 때도 있어요.
explain_en: It is easiest to learn as a set phrase, like '꼬임에 넘어가다' or '꼬임에 빠지다'. The related verb is '꼬드기다', and in everyday talk people also say '꼬시다'. The same word '꼬임' can also mean the state of a thread or rope being twisted.

examples.ko: 꼬질꼬질 때가 낀 운동화를 오늘 빨았어요.
examples.en: I washed my grubby, dirt-caked sneakers today.
The child came in all grubby and covered in dirt.
The old teddy bear has gotten all grubby.

examples.ko: 꼬질꼬질 때가 탄 이불을 주말에 빨 거예요.
examples.en: I'm going to wash the grimy blanket this weekend.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 꼬질꼬질 낡은 옷을 입고 있었어요.
examples.en: The kid was wearing dirty, worn-out clothes.

examples.ko: 하루 종일 뛰어놀았더니 얼굴이 꼬질꼬질 지저분해요.
examples.en: After running around all day, my face is grimy and messy.

explain: 오래 씻거나 빨지 않아 때가 타서 꾀죄죄한 모습에 써요. 사람, 옷, 인형 모두에 쓸 수 있지만 사람에게 직접 말하면 기분이 나쁠 수 있어요.
explain_en: It describes something shabby and grimy because it hasn't been washed for a long time. You can use it for people, clothes and toys, but saying it directly to a person can offend them.

examples.en: I haven't washed it for days, so the clothes are grubby.
Don't go out wearing those filthy sneakers.
The room is grimy, so I need to clean it.
After playing at the playground, the child's face was grubby.
Your hair looks grubby, so go wash it.
If you don't wash, you'll get grubby quickly.

explain: '더럽다'보다 오래 씻거나 빨지 않아 때가 타서 꾀죄죄한 느낌이에요. 뜻이 비슷한 '꾀죄죄하다'도 있어요. 부사 '꼬질꼬질'과 짝으로 외워 두세요.
explain_en: Compared with '더럽다', it has the feel of being shabby and grimy from not being washed for a long time. '꾀죄죄하다' is a similar word. It pairs well with the adverb '꼬질꼬질'.

examples.en: My younger sibling pinched my arm and left a bruise.

examples.ko: 자다가 볼이 꼬집히는 느낌이 들어서 깼어요.
examples.en: I woke up feeling like my cheek was being pinched.
The spot where my friend pinched me turned red.
Getting pinched that hard must really hurt.
I ran away quickly so my older brother wouldn't pinch me.
I got pinched by a friend while horsing around yesterday.

explain: '꼬집다'의 피동이라 누가 했는지는 '한테/에게'로 말해요. '친구가 내 팔을 꼬집었어요'처럼 능동으로 말할 수도 있어요.
explain_en: It is the passive of '꼬집다', and the person who did it is marked with '한테/에게'. You can also say it actively, as in '친구가 내 팔을 꼬집었어요'.

examples.ko: 시험지를 받기 전에 침을 꼴깍 삼켰어요.
examples.en: I swallowed hard before receiving the exam paper.

examples.ko: 케이크를 보니까 저도 모르게 군침이 꼴깍 넘어가요.
examples.en: Seeing the cake, I can't help but gulp with a watering mouth.

examples.ko: 아기가 분유를 꼴깍 삼키는 소리가 들려요.
examples.en: I can hear the baby gulping down its formula.
I gulped down the pill with water.

examples.ko: 목에서 꼴깍 소리가 날 만큼 크게 마셨어요.
examples.en: I drank so hard that my throat made a gulping sound.
I took a small sip of water with a gulp.

explain: '꿀꺽'보다 작고 가벼운 소리라 침을 삼키거나 조금 마실 때 잘 어울려요. '침을 꼴깍 삼키다'처럼 짝으로 외워 두세요.
explain_en: It is a smaller, lighter sound than '꿀꺽', so it suits swallowing saliva or taking a small drink. Learn it as a set, like '침을 꼴깍 삼키다'.

examples.en: I was so nervous that I swallowed hard.
I stayed up all night playing games.

examples.ko: 해가 꼴딱 넘어가기 전에 집에 가요.
examples.en: Let's go home before the sun sets.
I gulped down the medicine, but the bitter taste lingers.

examples.ko: 친구와 수다를 떠느라 날을 꼴딱 샜어요.
examples.en: I stayed up all night chatting with my friend.

examples.ko: 아이가 마지막 한 모금을 꼴딱 마셨어요.
examples.en: The child gulped down the last sip.

explain: '꼴깍'처럼 침이나 음식을 삼키는 소리로 쓰지만, '밤을 꼴딱 새우다'에서는 잠을 한숨도 못 자고 밤을 보낸다는 뜻이 돼요. 이 표현은 통째로 외워 두세요.

phrases.en: I stayed up all night studying for the exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잠을 한숨도 못 자고 밤을 보냈다는 뜻이에요. '밤을 새우다'를 더 생생하게 말하는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means you spent the night without sleeping at all. It sounds more vivid than plain '밤을 새우다'.

explain_en: Like '꼴깍', it is the sound of swallowing saliva or food, but in '밤을 꼴딱 새우다' it means spending the night without sleeping at all. Learn that expression as a whole.

examples.en: I bought a bag of small squid at the market.
A kkoltugi is much smaller than a regular squid.
Spicy stir-fried small squid goes well with rice.
The small squid sold at the mart looks fresh.
Salted small squid is savory and goes well with rice.

examples.ko: 오늘 저녁에는 꼴뚜기로 볶음을 해 먹을까요?
examples.en: Shall we stir-fry some small squid for dinner tonight?

explain: 오징어나 낙지와 비슷하게 생겼지만 훨씬 작은 바다 생물로, 볶음이나 젓갈로 먹어요. 속담 '어물전 망신은 꼴뚜기가 시킨다'에도 나와요.

phrases.example: 한 사람이 실수해서 우리 팀이 다 혼났어요. 어물전 망신은 꼴뚜기가 시킨다더니!
phrases.en: One person made a mistake and our whole team got scolded. Just like the proverb says!
phrases.nuance_ko: 못난 한 사람 때문에 같은 무리 전체가 욕을 먹거나 체면이 깎일 때 쓰는 속담이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb used when one poor performer makes a whole group look bad or get blamed.
phrases.en_equiv: one bad apple spoils the bunch

explain_en: It is a sea creature that looks like 오징어 or 낙지 but is much smaller, eaten stir-fried or salted. It also appears in the proverb '어물전 망신은 꼴뚜기가 시킨다'.

examples.ko: 어른이 길에서 떼를 쓰면 꼴사나워 보여요.
examples.en: An adult throwing a tantrum in the street looks unsightly.
I was so embarrassed to show such an ugly side of myself.
The clothes are wrinkled, so you look a bit shabby.
The way he ate was unpleasant even to look at.
Wouldn't it look bad to get angry after losing?
My hair was a mess and looked awful, so I put on a hat.

explain: '볼썽사납다'와 비슷하게 행동이나 모습이 보기 싫을 때 써요. ㅂ 불규칙이라 '꼴사나워요', '꼴사나운'으로 바뀌어요. 사람의 행동을 평가하는 센 말이라 직접 말하면 기분이 상할 수 있어요.
explain_en: Like '볼썽사납다', it is used when someone's behavior or appearance is unpleasant to see. It is a ㅂ-irregular, so it becomes '꼴사나워요' and '꼴사나운'. It is a harsh judgment of a person's behavior and can offend if said directly.

examples.en: Don't fidget with your fingers during class.

examples.ko: 아기가 잠에서 깨려는지 이불 속에서 꼼지락거려요.
examples.en: The baby seems to be waking up and is wriggling under the blanket.
It was cold, so I waited for the bus wiggling my toes.

examples.ko: 방에서 혼자 뭘 그렇게 꼼지락거리고 있어요?
examples.en: What are you fiddling with all by yourself in your room?

examples.ko: 손을 꼼지락거리는 걸 보니 긴장했나 봐요.
examples.en: Seeing you fidget with your hands, you must be nervous.
I dawdled in the morning and was late for school.

explain: '꼼지락거리지 말고 빨리 해'처럼 굼뜬 사람을 재촉할 때 자주 들어요. 손가락이나 발가락을 조금씩 움직이는 것 외에, 작은 일을 느릿느릿 만지작거리는 것도 가리켜요. 벌레나 작은 동물이 기어가는 느낌은 '꼬물거리다'가 더 잘 어울려요. '꼼지락대다'로 바꿔 써도 돼요.
explain_en: You often hear it when someone is told to hurry, as in '꼼지락거리지 말고 빨리 해'. Besides moving fingers or toes a little at a time, it also covers fiddling slowly with small tasks. For a bug or small animal crawling, '꼬물거리다' fits better. You can swap in '꼼지락대다' too.

examples.en: The baby lies there wiggling its fingers.

examples.ko: 아이는 방 한구석에서 꼼지락꼼지락 뭔가를 만들었어요.
examples.en: The child was making something slowly in a corner of the room.
I watched TV, wiggling my toes.

examples.ko: 새끼 고양이가 담요 속에서 꼼지락꼼지락 기어 나왔어요.
examples.en: The kitten wriggled its way out of the blanket.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 하루 종일 꼼지락꼼지락 화분을 손질하세요.
examples.en: Grandpa spends all day slowly tending to his flower pots.

examples.ko: 동생이 꼼지락꼼지락 딴짓만 해서 숙제를 못 끝냈어요.
examples.en: My sibling kept fiddling around and couldn't finish the homework.

explain: '꼼지락거리다'의 부사로, 손가락·발가락처럼 몸의 일부가 느리고 조금씩 움직이는 모습이에요. 작은 동물이나 벌레가 기어가는 느낌은 '꼬물꼬물'이 더 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is the adverb of '꼼지락거리다', describing a part of the body such as fingers or toes moving slowly and slightly. For the feel of a small animal or bug crawling, '꼬물꼬물' fits better.

examples.en: The child watches TV, wiggling their toes.

examples.ko: 앉아서 가만히 있지 못하고 계속 꼼지락대요.
examples.en: He can't sit still and keeps fidgeting.

examples.ko: 손가락을 꼼지락대는 걸 보니 심심한가 봐요.
examples.en: Seeing you wiggle your fingers, you must be bored.
Every time the baby wriggles in bed, it's adorable.

examples.ko: 책상 밑에서 뭘 그렇게 꼼지락대고 있어요?
examples.en: What are you fiddling with under the desk?
I fidgeted during class and the teacher looked at me.

explain: '꼼지락거리다'와 뜻이 같아서 어느 쪽을 써도 돼요. 둘 다 부사 '꼼지락꼼지락'과 짝으로 외우면 쉬워요. 해요체는 '꼼지락대요', 관형형은 '꼼지락대는'이에요.
explain_en: It means the same as '꼼지락거리다', so you can use either. It is easy to learn both together with the adverb '꼼지락꼼지락'. The polite form is '꼼지락대요' and the modifier form is '꼼지락대는'.

examples.ko: 엘리베이터가 사람으로 꽉 차서 꼼짝달싹 못 했어요.
examples.en: The elevator was packed, so I couldn't move an inch.

examples.ko: 폭설 때문에 도로의 차들이 꼼짝달싹 못 해요.
examples.en: Because of the heavy snow, the cars on the road can't budge.

examples.ko: 감기가 심해서 하루 종일 꼼짝달싹 안 하고 누워 있었어요.
examples.en: I had a bad cold, so I lay there all day without moving.

examples.ko: 허리를 다쳐서 꼼짝달싹 할 수가 없어요.
examples.en: I hurt my back and can't move at all.
Mom is watching me, so I can't make a single move.

examples.ko: 너무 무서워서 그 자리에서 꼼짝달싹 못 하고 서 있었어요.
examples.en: I was so scared that I stood there frozen, unable to move.

explain: '꼼짝'을 더 세게 말한 형태로, '꼼짝달싹 못 하다'처럼 거의 굳어진 표현으로 써요. 짧게 '꼼짝 못 하다'라고도 해요. '아내에게 꼼짝 못 하다'처럼 사람 뒤에 '에게'를 붙이면 상대에게 눌려 지낸다는 뜻이 돼요.
explain_en: It is a stronger version of '꼼짝' and is used almost as a fixed expression, '꼼짝달싹 못 하다'. The shorter '꼼짝 못 하다' is also common. With a person plus '에게', as in '아내에게 꼼짝 못 하다', it means being dominated by that person.

examples.ko: 아기가 침대 위에 꼿꼿이 서서 웃고 있어요.
examples.en: The baby is standing upright on the bed, laughing.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 연세가 많으신데도 허리를 꼿꼿이 펴고 걸으세요.
examples.en: Grandpa is old, yet he walks with his back held straight.
In an interview, sit with your back straight.

examples.ko: 선생님은 칠판 앞에 꼿꼿이 서서 우리를 바라보셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher stood upright in front of the board and looked at us.
The cat comes over with its tail held straight up.

examples.ko: 동생은 혼나는 중에도 고개를 꼿꼿이 들고 있었어요.
examples.en: Even while being scolded, my younger sibling held their head high.

explain: 허리나 몸이 굽지 않고 곧게 서 있는 모습이라 '곧게'보다 뻣뻣하고 힘 있는 느낌이에요. 형용사 '꼿꼿하다'는 '성격이 꼿꼿하다'처럼 굽히지 않는 태도를 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: It describes the back or body standing straight without bending, with a stiffer, firmer feel than '곧게'. The adjective '꼿꼿하다' is used for an unbending attitude, as in '성격이 꼿꼿하다'.

examples.ko: 아버지가 쌀자루를 자전거 꽁무니에 싣고 오셨어요.
examples.en: Dad brought the rice sack on the back of his bicycle.
I followed slowly, watching only the back of the car ahead.
The puppy trails right behind its mother.

examples.ko: 줄 꽁무니는 아직 문 앞에 있었어요.
examples.en: The tail end of the line was still at the door.
A lot of smoke is coming out of the back of the motorcycle.
I can see the end of the train far away.

explain: 자동차, 기차, 줄처럼 움직이는 것의 맨 뒤쪽이나 동물의 꼬리 쪽을 말할 때 써요. '꽁무니를 빼다'는 책임이나 위험한 일에서 슬쩍 물러난다는 뜻으로 써요.

phrases.example: 일이 어려워지자 친구가 슬그머니 꽁무니를 뺐어요.
phrases.en: When things got hard, my friend quietly backed out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 책임지거나 위험한 일에서 몰래 피해 물러날 때 쓰고, 조금 비겁하다는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone sneaks away from responsibility or danger, with a slightly cowardly feel.

explain_en: It means the very back of something moving, such as a car, a train or a line, or the rear end of an animal. '꽁무니를 빼다' is used for slipping away from responsibility or a risky situation.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 작은 일에도 따지는 꽁생원이에요.
examples.en: He is a petty person who argues even over small things.
His friends tease him for being narrow-minded.

examples.ko: 꽁생원처럼 굴지 말고 한번 웃고 넘어가요.
examples.en: Don't be so petty and just laugh it off.

examples.ko: 우리 아빠는 꽁생원이라서 농담도 잘 못 받아요.
examples.en: My dad is so petty that he can't take a joke.

examples.ko: 그런 일로 삐지다니 꽁생원이 따로 없네요.
examples.en: Sulking over that? You're a textbook petty person.

examples.ko: 꽁생원 같은 선배 때문에 회의가 늘 길어져요.
examples.en: Because of a petty senior, meetings always drag on.

explain: 마음이 좁아서 작은 일에도 신경 쓰고 오래 마음에 담아 두는 사람을 놀리듯 가리키는 말이에요. 비슷한 말로 '속이 좁다'가 있어요. 얼굴을 보고 말하면 기분이 상할 수 있어요.
explain_en: It teasingly refers to a narrow-minded person who worries about small things and holds grudges for a long time. A similar expression is '속이 좁다'. Saying it to someone's face can hurt their feelings.

examples.en: A sparrow walks along, wagging its tail.
A peacock's tail is truly magnificent.

examples.ko: 그 새는 꽁지에 하얀 털이 있어요.
examples.en: That bird has white feathers on its tail.
The chicken hid in the grass with only its tail showing.

examples.ko: 새가 꽁지로 균형을 잡으며 나뭇가지에 앉았어요.
examples.en: The bird landed on the branch, balancing with its tail.
I saw a long-tailed bird in the park.

explain: 새의 꼬리 쪽 깃털을 말해요. 강아지나 고양이 같은 동물에게는 '꼬리'를 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the tail feathers of a bird. For animals like dogs and cats, use '꼬리'.

examples.en: When spring came, the plum tree's buds burst open.

examples.ko: 꽃망울이 맺힌 걸 보니 곧 필 것 같아요.
examples.en: Seeing the buds form, they look like they'll bloom soon.

examples.ko: 아직 꽃망울만 있어서 벚꽃이 안 피었어요.
examples.en: There are only buds so far, so the cherry blossoms haven't bloomed.

examples.ko: 아침에 보니 꽃망울에 이슬이 맺혀 있어요.
examples.en: This morning I saw dew on the flower buds.
The little buds are opening one by one.

examples.ko: 장미 꽃망울은 아직 단단히 닫혀 있어요.
examples.en: The rose buds are still tightly closed.

explain: '꽃봉오리'와 같은 뜻으로 쓰고, 아직 피지 않았거나 막 피려는 꽃을 가리켜요. '꽃망울을 터뜨리다'는 꽃이 피기 시작한다는 말과 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It can be used the same way as '꽃봉오리', and refers to a flower that has not opened yet or is about to. It goes well with '꽃망울을 터뜨리다', meaning a flower starts to bloom.

examples.en: It's March, but it's still chilly because of the spring cold wind.
The chilly spring wind blew, so I took my scarf out again.
The cherry blossom petals are fluttering in the chilly spring wind.
The chilly flowering-season wind visits briefly in early spring.
I walked to school in the chilly spring wind.
Even in the chilly wind, the plum blossoms bloomed beautifully.

explain: 꽃이 필 무렵 이른 봄에 부는 쌀쌀한 바람이에요. 비슷한 시기의 추위를 가리키는 '꽃샘추위'와 함께 날씨 이야기에서 들을 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is the chilly wind that blows in early spring around the time flowers bloom. You can hear it in weather talk along with '꽃샘추위', which refers to the cold of the same season.
